summary: Requested the one remainder configuration the account still left unmeasured, and which the previous turn judged unbuildable: the removal of the leading node from a group whose remainder has two voters, with CheckQuorum enabled. Building it showed the earlier judgement wrong in an informative way - the two remaining voters keep answering the removed leader and their leases keep them from voting, so no replacement leader is needed for the scenario at all. The new harness (assurance_two_voter_checkquorum_test.go), verified in a clean copy of the module containing only that file, shows: the removal leaves node 1 leading voters (2 3) so the singleton shortcut cannot apply; three heartbeat rounds pass with node 2 and node 3 still followers at term 1 and therefore no new leader; the request is taken into readOnly.unconfirmedReads with two heartbeats broadcast; and after three further rounds the removed leader is still the leader at its own term while the request has been answered from its own frozen commit index - a round that counted the removed leader's own acknowledgement even though it is not one of the configuration's voters. The five comparisons are the singleton-free premise, the no-replacement premise, the accepted-request premise, the still-leading premise, and that witness (read_answered eq false, expected violated). Validation reports valid with an experiment created.
